provenance.sourceQuality: Reuters November 25, FT and AP corroborate Asian weakness; exact intraday timestamps unavailable. US cash data and paired yields are historical; no synchronized direct QQQ/SOX/VXN/WTI refresh. Open Watch unchanged at 178, newest events Nov 23.

editorial.marketOverview: Asian chip-heavy markets fell sharply Wednesday following Tuesday's US technology losses. Reuters reported renewed tariff fears alongside AI valuation concerns. US futures indications remain negative, but cash trading has not started.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the saved neutral assessment, the Asian selloff and renewed tariff investigation reporting weaken the Dell-led rebound scenario. The curated feed is unchanged; the new evidence comes from external reporting.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The divergence between strong AI server demand and weak chip prices suggests valuation and policy risks dominate near-term sentiment. Prior paired yields imply a positive 23.3 bp curve, but no fresh synchronized curve is available. Lower oil offers a partial inflation offset.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday has a bearish tilt ahead of PCE and GDP. Friday's shortened session raises liquidity risk; Monday is the next normal session to test whether chip leadership returns.
editorial.bullCase: Benign inflation and lower yields could trigger a rebound if semiconductor participation broadens and volatility eases. Dell demand provides fundamental support but is not sufficient alone.
editorial.bearCase: Further tariff escalation or sticky inflation could reinforce chip liquidation and extend QQQ weakness into Friday and Monday. Asian declines are observed, not a guarantee of US losses.
editorial.watchNext: Monitor PCE and GDP at 08:30 ET, actual tariff announcements, SOX relative to QQQ, breadth and VXN/VIX. Refresh paired yields and oil before drawing cross-asset conclusions.
